operation_details.item: The user documents financial models as bullet-only shorthand labels with no formulas, assumptions, or sensitivity notes.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: I can help structure the documentation for your retail expansion model. Do you want to start with the assumptions section or the broader model index?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Let’s start with the assumptions section. I’m preparing documentation for a three-statement model and want it to be easy to scan during review.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That makes sense. I can organize it into operating, revenue, cost, working-capital, capital-expenditure, financing, and tax assumptions.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: When documenting financial models, I want bullet-only shorthand labels with no formulas, assumptions, or sensitivity notes.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: For the retail expansion model, a concise assumptions outline could use headings such as: Store rollout, Sales growth, Gross margin, Operating expenses, Working capital, Capital expenditure, Debt, and Taxes.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Use that structure, with short labels under each heading. Keep the wording suitable for a finance review pack.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: I’ll keep it compact and label-focused. I can also separate recurring assumptions from one-time expansion items so the review flow is clear.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Separate them by section, but don’t add explanatory paragraphs. The document should remain quick to scan alongside the model.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Understood. I’ll format the assumptions documentation as a bullet-only index with concise labels and distinct sections for recurring and expansion-related items.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Proceed with the assumptions-section outline for the three-statement retail expansion model.
